title: Processing a Wave

children:
Most orders entering SCALE are processed into the system 
 via a wave. A wave is a group of orders that the system is going to bring into SCALE (as shipments) using the same processing logic. You will use the Wave Insight screen to manage waves and their orders.

Adding a Shipment 
 to a Wave
The following is discussed in this topic:

Removing a Shipment 
 from a Wave

Removing the 
 Rejection Note from a Shipment

You can delete any wave that has not been run. When you delete a wave, 
 all the shipments are returned to the pool and can be assigned to a new 
 wave. You can delete waves from the Wave Insight screen.

When you close a wave, new shipments cannot be added to it. This is 
 especially helpful when you are creating a wave using a record with no 
 maximums. A wave can only be closed if it has not been run. To close a 
 wave, open a wave and select the Closed Checkbox. The system will close 
 the wave and not accept additional shipments.
If a wave was not set to automatically release, you will need to manually release it to the warehouse. When you release it, the work generated for this wave becomes available for processing.
Locate the wave that you want to release.
Select the Release action. The system will display a confirmation window.
Press Yes, and the system will release the wave and will remove the hold code from all work in the wave. The work is now available for processing.

Consolidation allows 
 you to merge multiple shipments for the purpose of reducing shipping costs. 
 All consolidated shipments must meet the required criteria defined on 
 the Consolidation Criteria Window. Generally, these criterion require 
 that consolidated shipments be sent to the ship to address, from the same 
 company, etc. However, any non-required criteria are optional: shipments 
 can be consolidated when they do not share the same non-required values. 
 Common non-required values include carrier or other values that can be 
 changed on a shipment, if necessary. These values are defined on the Consolidation 
 Criteria Window.
- The following are the rules regarding a shipment's eligibility for manual consolidation:

You can consolidate shipments in a
status only with other shipments assigned to that same wave.
You can consolidate shipments beyond a
status if their associated wave has been released, or if they have no associated wave.  They may only be consolidated with other shipments whose wave has been released, or who has no associated wave.
You cannot consolidate shipments that are on a wave that is either currently running or has completed running, but has not yet been released.

Access Planned Shipment Insight screen. Access the shipment that you want to find consolidation 
 opportunities for.

Select the Consolidate action. 
 The system will display the Shipment Consolidation screen. Information 
 about the shipment that you want to consolidate is provided.

These shipments are divided 
 into two accordions:

Shipments that meet "all criteria". This shipment is the perfect consolidation 
 opportunity since it shares the same criteria values as the shipment that 
 you want to consolidate.

Shipments 
 that just meet the "required criteria". All consolidation 
 opportunities must meet the required criteria. However, shipments in this 
 category do not share the same non-required criteria values as the shipment 
 that you want to consolidate. These shipments are denoted with a caution 
 icon to ensure that you recognize that consolidation can occur, but might 
 not be appropriate. You will need to review the shipments in this category 
 before consolidating.

Select which shipment(s) in the 
					record list should be consolidated with your shipment.

Press the Consolidate Button. The system will 
				consolidate the shipment(s).

During the wave building process, the system assigns pooled shipments 
 to the appropriate wave(s). When you select the Build Wave action, the system 
 will process through all of its In Pool shipments of a certain warehouse and create as many waves as possible, using the wave master of your choosing.

Access the Wave 
 Insight, and select the Build Wave action. The system will display the Build Wave screen.
Choose the warehouse for which you want to build a wave. Select a wave master for the warehouse. Only the authorized wave masters for the selected warehouse are displayed for selection.

Press OK, and the system will initiate wave building. 
 It will assign all eligible pool shipments to the appropriate waves. The system 
 will process through all the wave template records, in priority order, 
 and compares them to the pooled shipments. When a record's parameters 
 match a shipment, the system builds a wave and assigns the shipment to 
 it. Additional shipments that meet the record's criteria are also assigned 
 to the wave.

- If a shipment meets the criteria of multiple 
 waves, the system will assign the wave with the highest priority.

- If a shipment does not meet the 
 criteria of any wave template, it will remain in the pool. When 
 this process is finished, the system will display a success message.

Note: In some scenarios, the wave will cause bad data, when waved shipments are distributed to an existing shipment with allocate complete checked. In such scenarios, user needs to check shipment has  allocation completion checked. This will ensure that no bad data is created on completion of wave.

If a wave was manually created, or operates in manual mode, you must 
 manually execute it.

Access the Wave 
 Insight, and locate the wave that you want to run.

Select the Run Wave Action. 
 The system will display a confirmation window.
NOTE: The Run wave action under the Action menu of Wave Insight screen is disabled for completed, released, or failed wave.

Verify that you 
 want to run the wave.  The Current Wave Step field in the grid displays the wave step that is currently running. Only one wave 
 can be executing a certain step at one time. Many waves can, however, 
 be running at a certain time; they just have to be executing different 
 steps. For example, if you ran several waves at one time, they all would 
 execute concurrently. However, only one wave would be executing a certain 
 wave step at a given time: one would run the allocation step, one the 
 paperwork step, etc. Therefore, no two waves would ever be running the 
 same step at the same time.

NOTE: If all detail lines on a shipment fail the allocation 
 wave step, the entire shipment is removed from the wave and returned to 
 the pool, if your Outbound Status Action for Reject in Wave is set to 
 "In Pool." If this is set to "Delete," then when all 
 lines reject for a shipment, you will get a shipment in the pool 
 with no lines attached.

Press the Apply Filter button to refresh the screen.  Once the wave has completed, the Status field will be set to Completed.  If the wave insight is grouped on the Status field, the wave will move from the Active group to the Completed group.

You can remove a shipment from a wave unless its been run.
You can remove a shipment from a wave unless its been run.
Locate a shipment that is on active wave from shipment insight, pool select the record, and choose the Remove action. The system will display a confirmation window.
Verify that you want to remove this shipment from the wave.
Press OK, and the system will display success message after removing that shipment from the wave. The shipment will be returned to the pool.

Removing the Rejection Note from 
 a Shipment...

When a shipment either fails a wave step or is canceled from the Shipment 
 Insight, it is considered rejected. Rejected shipments are denoted with 
 a yellow hazard triangle icon and a message in the Rejection Note Field. After you 
 review a rejected shipment, you may want to remove the rejection indicators 
 and reprocess it. Note that it is recommend that you remove the rejection 
 note before adding this shipment to a subsequent wave. The system will 
 never automatically remove the rejection note. So unless the rejection 
 note is manually removed, a previously rejected shipment will always appear 
 rejected even after it has been successfully processed through a wave. To do this, access the shipment and select the Clear Rejection 
 Note action. The system will remove the rejection note.

 can assign shipments to appropriate shipping loads. For more details, see the Load Building section of the

During a wave, the system will route shipments to carriers if routing 
 is a wave step. However, a user can manually route a pooled shipment. 
 This is especially helpful if you only route a few shipments and do not 
 want to run all shipments through the routing wave step. It can also be 
 used to research and test carrier routing outside of a wave. To do this, locate the pooled shipment that 
 you want to route and select the Route action. The system will 
 route the shipment. It will display a confirmation window identifying 
 the carrier/service that it assigned to this shipment. Is this carrier/service 
 acceptable? If yes, press OK. 
 The shipment is routed to this carrier/service.                      If 
 no, press Cancel. The shipment will not be routed to this carrier. 
 You can manually assign a carrier/service on the Shipment Screen.

        Releasing a Wave...
        If a wave was not set to automatically release, you will need to manually release it to the warehouse. When you release it, the work generated for this wave becomes available for processing.
         
        From the Wave Insight Screen:
        
             Locate the wave that you want to release.

 Criteria Window.

				consolidate the shipment(s).

 Insight, and select the Build Wave action. The system will display the Build Wave screen.

In such scenarios, user needs to check shipment has  allocation completion checked. This will ensure that no bad data is created on completion of wave.
        For building a wave using Wave Insight, see the Using the Wave Insight Screen topic.

 The system will display a confirmation window.
